SM_Frigate_Capstan.turns: about its own +Z (up): the drumhead heaves either way; the pawls (CapstanPawls) stay

SM_Frigate_Wheel.turns: about its own +X (forward along the axle): a positive turn takes the top of the wheels to port, and the ship's head to port (tiller ropes led as the period's ships led them); the standards (WheelStandards) and the tiller rope (TillerRope) stay: the barrel turns under the rope's turns, which look the same

SM_Frigate_Tiller.turns: the rudder's head and the tiller (one object, Tiller) about its frame's +Z (up the head's axis): a positive turn takes the tiller to starboard and the ship's head to port, as the wheel's positive turn does; the blade stays as built (its lower pintles stand off the axis)

long24.note: the gun deck's long 24-pounders. Each gun: its carriage's origin at carriage_x_m[pose] along its port's X (the carriage's axes the port's); the barrel at barrel_in_carriage_m in the carriage's frame, turned about its own Y (the trunnions) to the pose's elevation (positive raises the muzzle: a turn of -elevation about +Y); the quoin under the breech where quoin.x_m_by_deg puts it for that elevation (along the carriage's X, at quoin.z_m), but housed (out: the breech on the bed); the trucks at their origin_m (turn each about its Y as the carriage moves: radius truck_radius_m); the gun's own gear mesh for the pose and its irons, in its port's frame. Housed (the pose for sea, shown): the lid shut, the barrel at breech_on_bed_deg, its muzzle against the side over the port's head and lashed there. Run in: the lid shut or open, the barrel level; where the recoil brings it and it is loaded (slice 17 fires it from run out to here). Run out: open the lid to lid_open_deg (a turn about the lid's own +X); the gun elevates within run_out_elevation_deg (as far as the lid lets it where lid_open_deg is the lid's own limit, lid_max_deg)

elevation.note: with the quoin under the breech the barrel elevates from quoin_home_deg (its thick end under the base ring) to quoin_thin_deg (its thin end); drawn right out, the breech comes down on the bed at breech_on_bed_deg, the most it elevates (housed it lies so)

long24.lid_frame_note: lid_frame: the lid object's own frame (its origin and axes in the ship), the same for the lid's mesh: origin on the hinge axis midway between the hinges' knuckles, x along the axis (forward on the starboard side, aft on the port side, so both frames are right-handed and y points down), z out of the side; a turn of lid_open_deg about +x opens it. shut_lids: the lids with no gun behind them (the bridle ports), shut always, with their frames

carronade32.note: the quarterdeck's and forecastle's 32-pounder carronades: each gun's slide with its origin at fighting_bolt_x_m along its port's X, turned about its Z within train_deg; the bed's origin at bed_x_m along the slide and bed_z_m over the deck (the slide's top), the barrel at barrel_in_bed_m; the gun's own gear mesh for the pose and its irons in its port's frame (drawn with the slide square to the side)

guns_note: guns.json: the port frame's definition (frames_note), the shared meshes' own frames (meshes), the long guns' and carronades' port frames, poses and lid frames (metres there; this file's own entries are cm)

GunDeck.note: fourteen lanterns, unshadowed, and the cabin's, shadowed (its radius 4 m); the ports and hatches give daylight: no light probes below in this slice (the PC lane's to add if the frame allows)

BerthDeck.note: eleven lanterns and the wardroom's; the sick bay's, the steerage's (unshadowed, its reach would stop 0.81 m out at the wardroom's bulkhead: cast_shadows on its entry), the two forward crew's (unshadowed they would stop 3 m out at the sick bay's bulkhead, short of the fore messes) and the wardroom's cast shadows so they stop at their bulkheads, the rest are unshadowed with radius_m held short of the bulkheads between zones they would shine through (berthdeck.py lanterns). No light probes below in this slice

helm.note: the tiller (Decks/SM_Frigate_Tiller) turns about its own frame's +Z by the helm's degree (hard over hard_over_deg; a positive turn takes the tiller to starboard and the ship's head to port); at each whole degree the six rope parts take the frame in 'poses' (location_cm, rotation_xyzw in the ship's frame, a run's X scale); between degrees take the nearer pose or blend two; TillerRopeLeads and TillerSheaves stay. From docs/frigate-tiller's gundeck.json (tiller, tiller_ropes)
helm.moves: TillerEye_S/P and TillerWrap_S/P: set each frame to poses[k] (o, R: columns its axes in the ship) for the helm's degree (poses[k].helm_deg); TillerRun_S/P: likewise, its X scaled by scale_x (it runs along its own X from 0); the rest (TillerRopeLeads, TillerSheaves) stays. Between whole degrees take the nearer pose or blend two. The easing rope's slack (slack_in) is not drawn: its run stays straight
